topic: exercise type and dose for bone density after 40
title: The Simple Exercise That Helps Your Bones After 40
description:
A 2026 network meta-analysis in The BMJ pooled 124 randomised trials (18,429 adults aged 40 and over) to compare exercise types for bone density and fractures. Brisk walking or jogging showed benefits at the spine and both hip sites, with meaningful effects around 600 MET-minutes a week, about 2 to 3 hours of brisk walking. The certainty of the evidence was low to moderate.

Key takeaways:
• Brisk walking or jogging: better bone density at the lumbar spine, femoral neck and total hip
• Combined aerobic and resistance training: better bone density at the spine
• Mixed aerobic and mind-body exercise may lower fracture risk (low certainty)
• More is not always better: the dose-response curve looked like an upside-down U

scenes.narration: After forty, bone density slowly declines with age. A huge new study shows which exercise slows it best.
Researchers pooled 124 randomised trials, with more than eighteen thousand adults aged forty and up.
The standout was simple. Brisk walking or jogging improved bone density at the spine and the hips.
Mixing cardio with strength training also helped the spine.
How much? Meaningful benefits showed up at roughly two to three hours of brisk walking a week.
And more was not always better. The benefit curve looked like an upside-down U.
Mixed aerobic workouts and mind-body exercise may also lower fracture risk, though that evidence is weaker.
Overall certainty was low to moderate, so treat this as a strong nudge, not a guarantee.

Your move: aim for about two and a half hours of brisk walking a week. Pair each walk with something you already do, like lunch, so it sticks. Have osteoporosis or past fractures? Ask your doctor what's safe for you.
